Hi Kevin — great to hear the pilot dates. Short answers up front: yes, and probably. More detail below + a simple next step.

1) Reversible tier lift: we can create a one-cycle tier lift (Compact -> Core) that automatically reverts at the next billing boundary. That gives you reserved capacity, predictable latency SLAs, and the ability to avoid throttling during onboarding. We typically implement this as a "temporary commitment" amendment on the invoice so billing & quotas reflect the uplift and then step back automatically.

2) Feature-bridge (advanced reranking): we support per-route entitlements for a limited set of features. For pilots we can enable advanced reranking as an add-on (metered) on top of Compact for the pilot period without permanent seat changes. There are a few caveats: latency-sensitive models may require quantization changes and we may route some calls to a Core-optimized pool — we'll document any compatibility deltas.

3) Pilot discounts: we can offer a one-time pilot discount (we've proposed 30% off incremental uplift for the pilot window historically) in exchange for a short expansion commitment (e.g., 3–6 months post-pilot with a minimum throughput target). Ben (cc'd) handles approvals for deviations.

I attached a short proposal that sketches the two options (temporary tier lift vs. burstable capacity) and the estimated cost delta based on your usage file. Quick ask: can you share an expected peak tokens/day number or concurrent requests so we can size the reserved pool?

Next step: 30-min call tomorrow or Tuesday to agree on the amendment language and rollout mechanics. If you're comfortable, I'll draft the amendment and a short term sheet for Ben to sign off.

Thanks —
